cases.request: Explain the difference between the museum caption tool's --dry-run flag and its --apply flag. The man-page paragraph for both flags is pasted below this sentence and is the only source. The explanation is a short answer for one operator. Do not change the tool, open a second investigation, or launch anyone. Pasted paragraph: --dry-run prints the caption ids that would change and writes nothing; --apply writes those captions only after the same id list is shown.

Please spin up several researchers and a reviewer team to explain what a 'hold slip' means in our library email. The only source is this sentence from the style guide, already pasted: a hold slip tells a patron which branch has the reserved book and the date the hold expires. The answer is one paragraph. No files change, no extra sources are authorized, and no one else may be assigned.

Answer a patron question that needs two substantial, independent public sources: the town's posted meeting-notice statute, and the library's posted privacy notice. Each source has its own citation checklist and its own notes file. Neither investigation uses the other's notes. One editor writes the final answer after both citation files exist. Recommend the shape only. Do not publish the answer or contact the patron.

Produce two approved answer units for the library. First, a specialist writes the accepted glossary of hold, renewal, and fine. Second, a specialist writes the patron email, and that email may use only terms from the accepted glossary. The email is not ready until the glossary is accepted. One editor owns both handoffs. Do not send the email.

Write one sentence for the public grant report stating how long a library hold lasts. The sentence will be quoted outside the library. A separate checker, who did not draft the sentence, compares it with the accepted hold-period rule and rejects any figure that rule does not state. The drafter's own confidence is not the check. Do not submit the report.

Draft the public note about yesterday's book-drop outage from the accepted incident timeline, which is attached. An incorrect time or branch name would be sent to patrons. A second person who did not write the draft must check every factual sentence against that timeline and return concrete mismatches. The author does not grade their own draft. Do not post the note or open a new investigation.

Resume an approved multi-session FAQ after a context reset. The durable ledger already lists the accepted answers, the open question, and the stop date. One owner must finish the single remaining answer, which depends on the accepted ledger and cannot be split. There is no speed target and no benchmark. Do not add writers or republish completed answers.

Continue an approved multi-session town-hall FAQ from its durable ledger of accepted decisions and blocked questions. The current stage has two ready answer files: one for meeting notice and one for records retention. Their outlines and paths are already fixed, the paths do not overlap, and each file has its own citation check. One editor accepts both. This stage is delivery continuity, not a speed trial. Do not rerun finished questions.

Check two sentences that are already pasted here. Sentence A: the caption tool reads skills from the project skills directory. Sentence B: the paper's limitation is that the trial used one model snapshot. One owner can verify both sentences against the attached one-page excerpt. Separate research files would take longer to set up than the check. Produce a short cited note. Do not recruit investigators.

A coworker says the new invoice footer renders faster. The only evidence is two timings: 40 ms on a one-page invoice and 22 ms on a different three-page invoice. There is no correctness check and the inputs differ. The approved work is one owner's note of what is unknown. Do not run a benchmark, rent a machine, or claim a speedup.

Research two substantial public documents for the package-tracking webhook: the carrier's posted retry rules, and the posted signature scheme for webhook bodies. Each document needs its own citation log and its own notes file. Neither log depends on the other. One lead will write the combined research note after both logs are checked. Recommend the shape only. Do not implement the webhook.

The ticket says to research the webhook's retry rules and signature scheme in parallel. The signature memo is not allowed to invent terms: it must use the accepted glossary produced by the retry-rules memo, and that glossary does not exist yet. Keep one research owner and an accepted-artifact handoff. Do not start the signature memo early.

Two research memos for the cafeteria menu board are ready to write. The shared citation template, the question list, and the output paths are already accepted. One memo covers allergen labels and the other covers posted calorie rules. The paths are disjoint, neither memo waits on the other's prose, and each has its own citation check. One lead integrates the two files. Do not change the menu software.

A research note will be quoted in a public grant report: it claims the warehouse scanner's posted error rate. A wrong citation would misstate a public specification. The note's author must not be the person who checks it. A separate reader gets the original specification and the note, and marks each claim that the specification does not support. Do not submit the grant.

Resume an approved multi-session literature check of public captioning rules from its compact source ledger. One owner must resolve the single remaining disputed citation and record what is still uncertain for the next session. Nothing is being optimized, and no benchmark is needed or authorized. Do not open a second workstream or treat earlier notes as sufficient by themselves.

Research two substantial public sources for the cafeteria menu board before any combined note: the posted allergen-label statute, and the posted calorie-rounding rule. Each source has its own citation log and its own check. Neither log uses the other. One lead writes the combined note only after both logs exist. Do not change the menu software.

Change the warehouse screen's two button captions from 'OK' to 'Confirm' in slot_view.py and from 'Cancel' to 'Back' in scan_view.py. The interface is already fixed, the files are different, and each caption is one word. One owner can edit and check both in a few minutes. Do not assign a second implementer.

The photo-archive checksum loop has a correct baseline and a benchmark script. The owner asks only for a bounded description of one proposed change to the buffer size, and explicitly forbids experiments, extra workers, and any new compute. Recommend how one owner should assess that change. Do not run the benchmark or treat the baseline as permission to optimize.

Before any code change to the attendance export, investigate two substantial independent unknowns: which public CSV columns the district already documents, and which public timezone rules the export must follow. The sources and the note paths are disjoint, and each note has its own check. One lead reconciles both notes and only then may propose a build. Recommend the investigation shape. Do not write the export.

Two implementers own different files in the invoice tool: tax_table.py and footer.py. Both edits depend on a refund rounding rule that is not proved yet. The tax-table change must establish and show that rule, and the footer may change only after that demonstration is accepted. Separate files do not make the writes safe to run together. One integration owner. Do not ship invoices.

Two modules of the cafeteria menu board are approved to implement. The shared menu-item interface is already accepted. allergens.py and calories.py have disjoint write paths and separate acceptance checks, and neither module reads the other's uncommitted work. One integration owner merges the accepted results. Recommend the concurrent implementation. Do not launch it from this recommendation.

Implement an approved check that a warehouse scanner cannot read another site's inventory. A missed check would expose stock records across sites. A separate evaluator, who does not write the patch, must compare the observable reads with the written security criteria. The implementer's own test summary is not acceptance. Do not deploy the scanner.

Continue an approved multi-session change to the library hold email. The durable record lists the accepted template, the open unit, and a send that must not be repeated. One owner has the only ready unit, and it is coupled to that record. The goal is to finish the email correctly, not to make it faster. No benchmark is authorized. Do not resend mail or add workers.

Resume an approved multi-week migration of the package-tracking webhook. The checkpoint file is the source of what has been accepted. The current plan has two units: first replace the signature parser and accept its contract, then update the retry caller to that accepted contract. The caller is blocked until the parser artifact is accepted. One owner keeps the checkpoint. Stop at the agreed date. This is migration continuity, not a speed trial.

The attendance export fails only when the date is a district holiday. Two read-only investigations do not share notes: one collects the posted holiday calendar, and the other records which timezone parse_day uses. Each note has a check that does not need the other note. No fix is selected yet. One owner compares the notes before recommending a change. Do not edit the export in this recommendation.

Two warehouse commands fail: slot lookup and barcode reprint. Both failures are raised in the same parse_slot function, which the owner has open. A second person would reread that function. Reproduce both commands, fix the shared parser, and show both commands accepting the previously failing codes. Do not split the diagnosis.

The map-tile cache sometimes serves a stale tile. Two substantial read-only investigations are independent: one reads request timestamps into its own note, and the other reads the cache key derivation into a different note. Each note has a result that can be checked without the other. No patch is ready. One lead compares the notes before choosing a fix. Do not restart the tile service.

Diagnose the invoice footer's wrong total as two specialist units. The trace unit must finish and be accepted before the reproduction unit may build a fixture from that trace. The fixture is not ready now. One owner keeps the handoff. Do not change tax rates or send an invoice.

Two diagnostic fixtures for the menu board are ready to add. The shared failure report format is already accepted. The allergen fixture and the calorie fixture write disjoint files, neither needs the other's result, and each fixture has its own expected output. One owner integrates the two reports. Recommend the concurrent fixtures. Do not change production menu data.

A patch claims to stop the scanner from charging a deposit twice. Double charges are customer-visible. A separate evaluator must run the original failing sale, not the author's summary, and accept the patch only if that sale charges once. The author does not sign off on their own patch. Do not deploy the scanner.

Continue a multi-session diagnosis of the stale map tile. A durable incident file must survive context resets and records which evidence is accepted. The trace unit has to be accepted before a specialist may reproduce the cache-key failure from that artifact. One owner keeps the file and stops at the agreed time. This is diagnosis continuity, not a benchmark. Do not flush the production cache.

Resume the approved multi-session scanner incident. The durable ledger holds accepted traces and the open question. The current stage is a public incident paragraph that a separate evaluator must check against the ledger before the owner accepts it. Do not repeat finished traces, do not change the original failure criteria, and do not run a performance trial.

Review the six-line pluralization change before it is published on every museum caption. A wrong plural would be visible to visitors. A separate reviewer receives the wording list and the diff, not the author's note that it looks fine, and lists mismatches. Do not edit the files.

The changelog fixes the spelling of 'catalogue' in one line. The author asks to run a separate evaluator model because reviews should always be independent. The line and the dictionary entry are both in the request. One owner can see whether the spelling matches. Do not treat a second model as required, and do not edit anything else.

Review whether the town-hall FAQ may claim 24-hour hold notices. Two substantial evidence questions are independent: what the posted statute requires, and what the library's posted procedure actually says. Each question has its own notes file and its own check. Neither file uses the other. One reviewer writes the finding after both notes exist. Do not publish a finding yet.

Two review deliverables are approved. First accept a finding list for the signature parser. The retry-caller checklist may cite only findings from that accepted list, so it cannot be written yet. One review owner handles the handoff. Do not treat the checklist as ready.

Two compliance review reports are approved under one fixed rubric. One report covers the export package and the other covers the importer package. Their evidence folders and output paths are disjoint, neither report reviews the other report, and each report's findings can be checked alone. One owner synthesizes the two reports. Do not describe the pair as a generator and an evaluator.

Review the approved backup-restore runbook against the original recovery criteria. A missed step could drop a site's inventory snapshot. A separate evaluator receives the criteria and the runbook, not the author's checklist of why it passes, and records each unmet criterion. Do not run a restore.

Resume an approved multi-session review of the public grant claims from the accepted finding ledger. The current claim needs a separate evaluator against the original rubric before the owner accepts it. Keep the ledger of decisions and blocked claims. Do not reopen finished claims or change the rubric. No benchmark is authorized.

Review the claim that the scanner beeps only on unknown barcodes. Two evidence questions are independent: the posted beep specification, and the fixture log of known barcodes. The notes are disjoint and each check stands alone. One reviewer writes the finding after both notes exist. Do not change the scanner.

Choose between hold_until and expires_on for one date field in the library email. The existing field names are camel case with a verb, and both candidates are in the request. The choice is small and reversible. Give one design recommendation. Do not implement it or delegate it.

The epic title is 'multi-week design program' for the menu board. The only approved decision is whether the allergen icon is a triangle or a circle. The style guide snippet is pasted here and says warning icons are triangles. Nothing must be stored for a later session, and no second designer is useful. Recommend the icon. Do not start a program.

Design the archival filename for photo checksums, but first resolve two substantial independent unknowns: the public accessibility rules for the filename, and the public retention period that must appear in it. The sources and note paths are disjoint and each note is checked alone. One designer reconciles both notes before choosing the pattern. Recommend the investigation. Do not rename files.

Two design specialists are approved. The first produces an accepted field list for the hold email. The second produces the wire order of those fields and cannot start until the field list is accepted. One design owner checks the handoff. Do not implement the email.

Design the scanner's low-battery icon, but first resolve two substantial independent unknowns: the posted contrast rules for the device screen, and the posted icon-size rules. The sources and note paths are disjoint, and each note is checked alone. One designer reconciles both notes before choosing the icon. Do not draw the final asset.

Propose an approved design for rotating the webhook signing key, including what happens during the overlap window. A wrong overlap would reject valid carrier calls. A separate evaluator receives the original uptime criteria and the design, and tries concrete overlap cases. The designer's narrative is not evidence. Do not rotate any key.

Continue an approved multi-session design of the photo archive. The durable decision log is the record of accepted constraints. The current units are ordered: the retention field list must be accepted before the filename pattern may use it. One designer keeps the log and stops at the agreed review date. Do not rename stored files and do not run a performance comparison.

The owner has explicitly authorized a bounded comparison of two photo-grid layouts. A correct baseline layout, a fixed set of the same albums, and a stop after six measurements already exist. One designer must name the current bottleneck before any isolated trial, keep the albums comparable, and stop at the cap. Do not buy hardware or treat a faster number as permission to change the acceptance criteria.

project_case.request: Recommend a project plan for a library hold-notice mailer with text and HTML output. Do not implement it. First investigate two independent public requirements: the posted hold-period rule and the posted privacy rule for patron names. One owner then settles the small shared subject-line contract directly. An accepted notice template must exist before a substantial HTML renderer may use it; separate files do not remove that wait. After the template and the field list are accepted, the text renderer and the HTML renderer can be built in disjoint directories. A separate evaluator checks the mailer against the original acceptance. A later approved continuation has one ready coupled unit, must keep a durable send ledger, and is not a speed trial. Reselect when evidence changes without changing the original acceptance or adding features, vendors, file writes, launches, or a live send.
required_milestones: later session with a send ledger
required_invariants: HTML renderer waits for the accepted template
the plan does not authorize a live send
the later session is not a benchmark
no speed trial without a new authorization

stages.ready_when: The hold-period rule and the privacy rule have separate sources, notes, and checks.
Both requirement notes are accepted and one owner can settle the short subject line.
The template unit can start, and the HTML renderer stays blocked until that template is accepted.
The field list is accepted and both renderers have disjoint directories and separate checks.
The integrated mailer can be checked by someone who did not build it, against the original acceptance.
The continuation has a durable send ledger, one coupled ready unit, and no speed target.

limits: heldout-v2 is the release routing pack. Expected fields and stage labels are evaluation data, not a production keyword classifier, and they stay withheld from fresh host inputs. The answers file records why each label was chosen and is not model input. Offline scoring checks string equality with these labels. It does not judge whether a recommendation was wise. Tune routing guidance only on the dev pack tests/fixtures/routing-scenarios.json. Score this pack once per release. Do not read this pack while editing skills/aic.
